# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Weekly Report (Feb 1 - 7, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, development focused on refining the core infrastructure of the Superchain, specifically addressing synchronization logic and registry accuracy. Key activities included the integration of SaferSafes addresses across both Sepolia and Mainnet configurations to enhance the ecosystem's tooling. Significant technical discussions also took place regarding the reliability of Execution Layer (EL) sync in `op-node` and the potential for `op-supernode` to provide "super roots" for unsafe data. These efforts underscore a continued commitment to protocol security and the robustness of cross-chain interoperability.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
The primary technical output this week involved updates to the registry's configuration files to support ecosystem partners and improve chain metadata.

### Superchain Configuration Updates
The registry was updated to include the SaferSafes address, ensuring that this infrastructure is correctly mapped across the Superchain ecosystem.
*   **SaferSafes Integration:** Added the SaferSafes address to `superchain.toml` files for both Sepolia and Mainnet environments ([#1197](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1197)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week saw a mix of critical bug resolutions and deep technical debates regarding the future of Superchain data availability and synchronization.

### Closed Issues
*   **op-supernode L1 Polling:** Resolved a bug where `op-supernode` failed to receive L1 head updates when configured with an HTTP L1 RPC URL ([#19012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19012)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Synchronization & Correctness:** Ongoing discussions regarding `op-node` ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/17631)) focused on the risks of marking EL Sync targets as finalized prematurely. Contributors are debating the merits of Snap Sync with `op-geth` versus `op-reth` and exploring derivation strategies to verify alignment with the unsafe chain.
*   **SuperRoots for Unsafe Data:** A new proposal ([#19059](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19059)) explores allowing `op-supernode` to return "super roots" for unsafe data. This would provide a mechanism for accessing data even when verified or safe data is not yet available at a specific timestamp.
*   **Interop Testing:** Issue [#18616](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/18616) was reopened to track skipped acceptance tests for interop proofs. The `TestInteropReadiness` remains disabled pending support for explicit output roots from the super DG.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by high-level technical architecture discussions involving several core contributors. Notable exchanges between @trianglesphere, @axelKingsley, and @sebastianst regarding EL Sync UX highlight a rigorous peer-review process for protocol-level changes. Additionally, the reopening of interop-related testing issues by @ajsutton indicates a focused effort on maintaining high testing standards as the Superchain moves toward more complex cross-chain features. The successful merge of the SaferSafes PR demonstrates the registry's role as a living document for the growing ecosystem.
